about.description:
I'm an **Artificial Intelligence** student at Universidade Santa Cecília (Brazil), and I build web and AI projects with **Python**, **TypeScript** and **JavaScript**: an agent that reads resumes and matches them to job openings, a platformer that runs in the browser, and a meeting room booking system with React and PostgreSQL.

I work with **AI-assisted development** (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) from prototype to deploy, using prompt engineering to plan, write, test and review code. Everything I build is public on GitHub.

I'm also an HR Apprentice at the Shared Services Center of **Coca-Cola FEMSA**. That high-volume routine (ServiceNow tickets, spreadsheets, documents) is where many of my ideas come from: repetitive processes that can be automated.

projects.title: VivAI+
projects.description: AI agent for resume screening. It takes PDF or DOCX files, extracts the candidate's data and uses the Gemini API to match the profile against Viva+'s open positions. The analysis ignores sensitive data and evaluates skills only, and the history is stored in a cloud database. The architecture was designed not to crash during usage spikes.

projects.title: HR Agent for WhatsApp
projects.description: AI agent for HR support on WhatsApp. It answers questions about benefits, badges and vacation based on company documents, using RAG on Postgres, and hands off to a person when it cannot find the answer. Sensitive topics never get an AI reply, and new answers only enter the knowledge base after human approval. It understands voice messages, stays within the free message limit and scored 31 out of 31 questions in its evaluation. Study project with a fictional company: the demo simulates delivery through WhatsApp.

projects.title: Sankofa: Paths of Resistance
projects.description: 2D platformer that runs in the browser, about the history of Black resistance in Brazil, made for Black Awareness Month (November). Phaser 3 with strict TypeScript and Vite. Every sprite, background and song is generated in code, with no image or audio files: textures come from text-based pixel grids and the sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API. It features coyote time, jump buffering, capoeira moves in a state machine, touch controls and a custom tool that simulates the jumps to check that every level can be completed.

projects.title: MeetKof
projects.description: Internal meeting room booking system. Calendar with monthly, weekly and daily views, bookings without time conflicts (enforced in the database and in the API), an admin panel for rooms and users, configurable booking rules and an audit log of who changed what. Frontend in React 19 with TypeScript, Tailwind and TanStack Query; backend in Node.js with Fastify and PostgreSQL on Supabase; tests with Vitest.

projects.title: Digitalize
projects.description: Web app to digitize and organize office documents. Create folders, scan with the phone camera using image processing that fixes the lighting and gives the result a real-scanner look, search inside folders and protect access with a login. Responsive interface for desktop and mobile.

projects.title: Guess the Pokémon
projects.description: Guessing game with a TV game show vibe: find out the randomly drawn Pokémon from its silhouette and hints. It uses the PokeAPI, and each wrong guess unlocks a new hint and reveals a bit more of the image. Built as a hands-on assignment for the Programming Techniques with AI course at Universidade Santa Cecília. The game itself is in Portuguese.

projects.title: Viva+ Corporate Website
projects.description: Website for Viva+, a corporate wellness company (health, leisure, culture and team integration). It presents the company, its departments, team and projects, and includes an admin panel so the team can update the content without coding. The website is in Portuguese.

projects.title: This portfolio
projects.description: The site you are looking at. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework: all the content lives in JSON files (one per language) editable through a Decap CMS panel, the repositories and the contribution chart come live from the GitHub API, and it deploys automatically to Netlify on every push.
